evidence.text: The entry describes 場 as 从土, 昜聲, and cites 說文. It explains the original sense as level ground used for ancient sacrifice. The site lists a seal-script image for 場 but no oracle-bone or bronze examples in its entry.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 場

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry reproduces the 大徐本 explanation: “祭神道也。一曰田不耕。一曰治穀田也。从土，昜聲.” It records 塲 as a variant and cites Dunhuang俗字譜 examples plus later lexicographic attestations. Its entry lists oracle-bone and bronze reference works as unavailable, so those do not establish an early inscriptional sequence here.
evidence.title: 場 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.text: The entry cites 《孟子·滕文公上》 for a 場 associated with sacrifice at Confucius’s tomb; 《漢書·郊祀志》 for altar and cleared-ground wording; 《詩·豳風·七月》 and 《周禮·地官》 for the grain-drying floor and 场圃. It also gives later/extended examples for a general place or battlefield from 《戰國策·秦策一》, a deer’s resting place from 《小爾雅·廣獸》, figurative domain from 《文選》, and a classifier use in Tang Li Bai and 《宋史》. These are quoted textual loci; the page does not date the individual attestations within those works or establish every semantic link historically.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 場

evidence.text: The entry says oracle-bone and early bronze forms of 昜 comprise 日 and 丂, interpreting 丂 as a tree branch; later bronze forms add 彡 for rays. It proposes sunshine as the original graphic sense and identifies 昜 as an early form underlying 陽 and 暘. This is the database’s paleographic interpretation of 昜, not evidence that 場 itself is attested in oracle-bone writing.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 昜

evidence.source: 韻典網, 上古音系 (Zhengzhang Shangfang system)
evidence.text: Its search record gives 場 as l'aŋ and marks 昜 as its sound component; it gives 昜 as laŋ. These are reconstructions in Zhengzhang Shangfang’s Old Chinese system, not direct recordings of speech. In Middle Chinese, the dictionary record gives 場 as 直良切, 澄母, 陽韻, level tone, with Baxter transcription drjang. The rhyme and syllable shape support a phonetic role, though the initials are not identical in the cited reconstructions.
evidence.title: 檢索 — 韻典網

evidence.source: 韻典網, 上古音系 (Zhengzhang Shangfang system)
evidence.text: The 昜 search record gives Middle Chinese 與章切, 以母, 陽韻, level tone, Baxter transcription yang; its Zhengzhang Old Chinese reconstruction is laŋ. The entry separately reports 昜’s ancient senses and scripts; readings and graphic origin should not be conflated.
evidence.title: 檢索 — 韻典網

evidence.text: The 場 entry gives Mandarin cháng/chǎng and Middle Chinese categories 澄母, 陽韻, level tone, open division III; the dossier separately supplies Cantonese coeng4. The sound-component entry gives Mandarin yáng and Middle Chinese 以母, 陽韻, level tone. The difference in modern initials does not erase the historical rhyme correspondence.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 場

evidence.field: 昜 graphic origins and later component role
evidence.text: The phonetic-series index groups 場 with many 昜-series characters. Its 昜 entry instead treats 昜’s own ancient composition and origin, listing it as a sound component in characters including 場. Thus uncertainty or debate about what 昜 originally depicted does not by itself undermine its documented later phonetic use in 場.
evidence.title: 聲符表 — 上古音系 — 韻典網

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The dictionary links 場 with variant shapes, including 塲, and cites historical variant records. It does not provide evidence on this page for the claim that simplified 场 specifically developed from a cursive form of 場. External results for that claim were mostly non-primary summaries or isolated calligraphy listings; the precise historical path remains unverified here.
evidence.title: 場 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: 中國哲學書電子化計劃, character dictionary
evidence.text: The search result reports 場’s modern Mandarin cháng/chǎng, Cantonese coeng4, Tang reading *djhiɑng, 說文’s analysis, and 《廣韻》’s gloss for a ritual place and grain-processing ground. The opened page returned an internal fetch error, so these details are retained only as search-result leads, not as inspected page evidence.

gaps: No inspected source in this research established an oracle-bone or bronze form of 場 itself. The CUHK 場 entry has no oracle-bone/bronze examples; the MOE variant page lists relevant specialist paleographic reference resources as unavailable. Tertiary claims that 場 occurs in oracle-bone script were not accepted without primary support.

The precise graphic route from traditional 場 to simplified 场, including the dossier’s cursive-adaptation claim, remains unverified by a strong inspected primary source. Shape similarity and general facts about cursive-based simplification do not establish this character’s path.

The semantic progression from ritual cleared ground to threshing floor, general venue, figurative domain, and classifier is plausible from cited lexicographic attestations, but surviving quotations do not fully document intermediate chronology or prove every link. A gloss list alone cannot establish that sequence.
The date of the earliest occurrence of 場 in an extant manuscript or inscription was not established. Classical loci quoted by the university database are not dated precisely on the page.

The interpretation of 昜’s own earliest components and referent remains an account by the CUHK database; its cited 丂-as-branch analysis is attributed to 屈萬里, with other interpretations noted. This uncertainty does not negate 昜’s independently supported phonetic role in 場.

No whole-character phonetic borrowing claim is supported. The available evidence treats 土 as semantic and 昜 as phonetic; no donor word, independently recoverable depicted-object name, or borrowing chronology is established or required for that component analysis.

The sound comparisons use Zhengzhang Shangfang’s Old Chinese system and Middle Chinese rhyme-dictionary categories. Reconstructions are scholarly models, not direct pronunciation recordings; the initial correspondence between 場 and 昜 is not exact in the cited system.

The CText page could not be opened, the Sinica query interface did not expose character results in page text, and a Ministry PDF search result could not be opened due to redirect loop. Those failures are recorded rather than treated as inspected evidence.
